Your first program

Open the BASIC Computer’s index.html directly, or open it from BASIC Lab on your local site. The Observatory example is already loaded. Type RUN, enter a name, then type CONT after STOP.

Start from a blank page

Choose New blank program. If you have a program, export it before accepting replacement. Keep Microsoft 8K selected for this tutorial. Type each line at READY and press Enter:

10 INPUT "YOUR NAME";N$
20 PRINT "HELLO, ";N$
30 END

Type LIST to inspect it, then RUN. At INPUT, your response is data for the program, not a command. Type HELP at READY to see the environment commands.

Change a line

Type EDIT 20. Move with Left/Right or Home/End; Enter commits, Escape cancels. Keep the line number. Typing a numbered line replaces that line; a number alone deletes it. You can select a line in the latest small LIST output, but the transcript itself stays read-only.

Write several lines

Open Source editor. Its gutter counts text rows; BASIC line numbers remain part of your source. Apply source commits without running. Apply & run explicitly commits and executes. Escape or Cancel changes discards the draft. Tab leaves the editor. Closing the section keeps your draft. Apply or cancel before changing source elsewhere.

Continue exploring

Browse examples gives you seven original programs. Loading one selects its documented language profile but does not run it. Try Countdown, then the arrays example. The terminal remains the primary way to issue RUN, LIST, STOP and CONT.
